item.title: Hosts Ba draw tough pool for BOG
item.description: THE Extra Supermarket Battle of the Giants pool stage is set for a fierce contest after four of the Extra Premier League’s top-ranked teams were drawn together in Pool B. The pools were drawn based on the standings after Round 14, which served as the qualifying round for the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
THE Extra Supermarket Battle of the Giants pool stage is set for a fierce contest after four of the Extra Premier League’s top-ranked teams were drawn together in Pool B.

The pools were drawn based on the standings after Round 14, which served as the qualifying round for the tournament.

In pool A are Labasa, Nasinu, Suva, Navua and in pool B are Ba, Rewa, Lautoka and Nadi.

Fiji Football Association chief executive Mohammed Yusuf described Pool B as the “pool of death”, with two teams set to exit the competition after the pool stage.

“Two top teams will exit the competition after pool games,” Yusuf said.

Pool B features teams ranked first, second, fourth and seventh in the Extra Premier League, setting up a demanding battle for the two semi-final places.

Yusuf said the strength of the pool means every match will carry the intensity of a final.

“The pool games in Pool B is like a final every day. On Friday, Saturday and Sunday afternoon, you will see a top-class battle between the top teams,” he said.

With only two teams able to progress from each pool, the margin for error will be small for the sides considered among the leading contenders.

Yusuf believes the draw could produce a high-quality tournament, with the strongest teams expected to face each other before the semi-finals.

Meanwhile, the other pool is expected to provide a more evenly matched contest, giving teams there an opportunity to battle for the remaining semi-final places.

The Battle of the Giants will therefore provide an early test for the leading Extra Premier League sides, with Pool B likely to determine which contenders can handle the pressure and progress to the final stages.

The 2026 BOG will take place at the 4R Govind Park Stadium in Ba, September 4-6 for the knockout stages and September 12-13 for the finals.

item.title: Navua eyes stronger BOG campaign
item.description: NAVUA FC Coach Rodeck Singh wants the side to turn around its inconsistent league form before they begin their Battle of the Giants (BOG) campaign. Navua FC finished eighth in the Extra Premier League, with Singh admitting that their inconsistent form has been a concern throughout the season.
item.content:encoded:
NAVUA FC Coach Rodeck Singh wants the side to turn around its inconsistent league form before they begin their Battle of the Giants (BOG) campaign.

Navua FC finished eighth in the Extra Premier League, with Singh admitting that their inconsistent form has been a concern throughout the season.

“We are not consistent, we win, we lose, we draw. In that form, we cannot take it to the tournament. We need to be winning and continuously winning to see ourselves progress,” Singh said.

Singh believes the BOG will provide a different challenge, with Navua drawn in a pool he describes as tricky and competitive.

“You cannot underestimate any team in that pool. It’s going to be tough for the competition. Every team has been improving,” he said.

He pointed to Nasinu’s league performance as an indication of the quality Navua will face, saying his players must be ready to produce top-quality football if they are to progress from the pool.

Navua still have one league match against Nasinu before turning their attention fully to the BOG.

Singh said the team’s expectation remains the same, to improve on its previous BOG performance and push all the way to the final.

“We are preparing, but we have one league game left with Nasinu that we are concentrating on. And then after that we shift focus to BOG,” he said.

Singh is also calling on Navua supporters and the business community to rally behind the team during its preparations and throughout the tournament.

He believes strong support from the fans could provide the players with an added boost as they look to overcome their league inconsistency and make a deeper run in the BOG.

item.title: Fijiana confident of levelling series against SA
item.description: THE Vodafone Fijiana XV is determined to bounce back and level its two-Test series against South Africa when the sides meet at Churchill Park in Lautoka today. Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says the team has taken valuable lessons from the opening Test and believes a much-improved performance can put Fiji in contention for a series-levelling victory.
item.content:encoded:
THE Vodafone Fijiana XV is determined to bounce back and level its two-Test series against South Africa when the sides meet at Churchill Park in Lautoka today.

Fijiana XV head coach Willie Walker says the team has taken valuable lessons from the opening Test and believes a much-improved performance can put Fiji in contention for a series-levelling victory.

Walker identified consistency and effort as the biggest areas the Fijiana needed to improve after the first Test.

“There were a few lessons to take from that first game. Probably the biggest one we’ve taken out of it is effort. We must make sure we put in an 80-minute effort and not just an effort that’s just going in fits and bursts,” Walker said.

The Fijiana have worked hard during the week to address those shortcomings, with particular emphasis placed on their effort levels in both attack and defence.

“The biggest thing we’ve worked on this week is just our efforts both in attack and defence and hopefully it will translate on the field tomorrow,” he added.

Defence has also been a major focus, with Walker stressing the need for a stronger attitude from his players.

“It was more an attitude thing as well. Again, we’ve worked pretty hard on that this week. We expect the girls to put up a better showing tomorrow because of it.”

Fijiana fans can also expect several changes to the starting line-up, with local players rewarded for their performances in the Marama and Ranadi competitions.

“We’ve made a few changes to the team. We’ve brought in a couple of players that have performed in the local Marama and Ranadi competition.

“So that’s a reward for our local players and we feel that they’re ready to step up into this environment.”

Despite the changes, Walker said the team would maintain its core group and was confident the players could deliver a stronger showing.

For Walker, the objective is more than simply making the second Test competitive.

The Fijiana genuinely believe they can level the series.

“Again, last week was something that wasn’t expected from all of us. So yeah, we expect to go out and do a better performance and yeah, we’re definitely going into levelling the series.”

With a strong home crowd expected at Churchill Park, Walker has called on supporters in the West to get behind the Fijiana.

“We’re going to put on a show. Expect a better performance from us. Expect a better showing from the girls and again, we hope for a positive result,” he concluded.

item.title: Super Deans finals in Suva next week
item.description: THE Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union finals will be played at HFC Stadium in Suva on August 22, setting the stage for a grand finale after tomorrow’s highly anticipated semi-final battles across Lautoka and Suva. A Fiji Rugby Union official confirmed the final venue and date to this newspaper.
item.content:encoded:
THE Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union finals will be played at HFC Stadium in Suva on August 22, setting the stage for a grand finale after tomorrow’s highly anticipated semi-final battles across Lautoka and Suva.

A Fiji Rugby Union official confirmed the final venue and date to this newspaper.

Before the finalists are decided, the spotlight turns to Churchill Park in Lautoka and Buckhurst and Bidesi Parks in Suva today, where schools will battle for places in the national finals.

The semi-finals are expected to draw strong support, with parents, students and rugby fans preparing to turn up in their school colours and create a vibrant atmosphere around the venues.

Among the Western teams carrying high hopes into today’s action is Ba Methodist High School U17, which faces Ratu Kadavulevu School in a highly anticipated semi-final.

The encounter will be the second meeting between the two schools this season after Ba Methodist defeated RKS in the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby League final.

Ba Methodist will be hoping for a similar result tomorrow, but the Nailaga-based school knows it will face a determined RKS outfit seeking to turn the tables.

Ba Methodist booked its semi-final spot after a hard-fought 22-19 victory over Gospel High School in the quarter-final at Tavua last Saturday.

The young Ba side showed composure and resilience in a match that went down to the wire, with Gospel High continuing to apply pressure until the final whistle.

Ba Methodist managed to withstand the late challenge and protect its narrow lead to secure its place in the last four.

The school’s preparation has also been boosted by the establishment of the Ba Rugby Academy, while several of its players are currently part of the Fijian Drua Development programme.

Ba Methodist High School principal Azam Ali said discipline would remain a key focus for the players.

“My main message to the players was to always maintain discipline. I have faith in this team,” Ali said.

Ali said the semi-final appearance was a significant achievement for the school, particularly after previous campaigns ended at the quarter-final stage.

item.title: BMHS make history
item.description: Ba Methodist High School have become the first school in Ba to reach the semi-finals of a Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union competition with the U17s defeating a strong Gospel High 22-19 last weekend. “We can’t be sure, but we don’t think any other school in Ba has made it this far before in the long history of the competition,” BRU Secretary Gaby Kautoga said. “Several have made the quarter-fina
item.content:encoded:
Ba Methodist High School have become the first school in Ba to reach the semi-finals of a Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union competition with the U17s defeating a strong Gospel High 22-19 last weekend.

“We can’t be sure, but we don’t think any other school in Ba has made it this far before in the long history of the competition,” BRU Secretary Gaby Kautoga said. “Several have made the quarter-finals but not the last four.”

The Saints U17s face the might of RKS in today’s semi-final which kicks off at midday at HFC Bank Stadium.

Last year’s BMHS U16s reached the quarter-finals and have gone unbeaten this season with additional input from eight members of the Ba Rugby Academy.

“The school’s U15s also excelled this year and reached the FSSRU Quarterfinals,” Kautoga noted. “It’s a good sign that we have young players coming through the ranks.”

The BRU has made a big effort in the last 12 months to work more closely with the nine secondary schools in the district.

“In the past, things have been a bit disjointed,” Kautoga admitted. “Schools have tended to work in isolation.”

“Ba Rugby reached out to all the schools at the end of last year, provided the opportunities for the teachers to get their coaching certificates and offered our top resources coaches for those who wanted help.”

Kautoga noted that the response was mixed.

“Ba Methodist has worked with us hand-in-hand, and some of the others made use of the clinics and our coaching assistance.”

“But we suspect that many schools aren’t really aware of the level of coaching required to take up a team to the knockout stages. You can’t rely on talent alone.”

With the new regulations on double registration allowing players in the district to join another school once their team has been eliminated, six BMHS U18 players joined Ra High.

“Five of them started in last week’s historic victory over defending champions RKS,” Talatala Gaby said. “These are players who went through our U17s programme and trials last year.”

Ra High face Suva Grammar In today’s Dean’s Semifinals at Churchill Park as the main game after the Fijiana-Springbok Women’s Test match.

item.title: NETBALL FIJI REVIVAL I Northern rally sparks netball revival
item.description: The M-PAiSA Netball Fiji Rally is giving grassroots netball a major boost, with the strong response to the inaugural Northern leg in Savusavu sparking calls for the event to become an annual fixture. More than 30 teams took part in the Northern Rally last Friday, highlighting the depth of interest and talent in grassroots netball outside Fiji’s traditional competition centres.
item.content:encoded:
The M-PAiSA Netball Fiji Rally is giving grassroots netball a major boost, with the strong response to the inaugural Northern leg in Savusavu sparking calls for the event to become an annual fixture.

More than 30 teams took part in the Northern Rally last Friday, highlighting the depth of interest and talent in grassroots netball outside Fiji’s traditional competition centres.

For many young players, community competitions such as the M-PAiSA Rally are where their netball journeys begin. The opportunity to compete in a structured tournament provides players with valuable exposure, while giving them a platform to develop their skills and gain experience in competitive netball.

The rally has also brought communities together, with players, families and supporters turning out to celebrate the sport. The response in Savusavu has been particularly encouraging, with growing calls from the Northern community for the rally to return each year.

For Netball Fiji, that response reflects the wider objective of its revival ,strengthening the sport from the grassroots up and creating more opportunities for players across the country.

The partnership with M-PAiSA, operated by Digital Financial Services Pte Limited, a owned subsidiary of Vodafone Fiji, is also helping to strengthen that pathway. The rally marks M-PAiSA’s first sporting event sponsorship and represents an investment in creating opportunities for young women and men to participate in competitive sport, develop their abilities and potentially pursue professional sporting careers.

M-PAiSA General Manager Digital Financial Services, Shailendra Prasad, said the Northern Rally had provided strong momentum for the partnership.

“The Northern Rally was a successful start to our partnership with Netball Fiji. We expect even greater participation in the Central and Western rallies. This is about giving more players the opportunity to compete, develop their skills and take the next step in their netball journey.”

The momentum generated in the North now moves to the Central Division, with the next rally scheduled for Saturday, August 15, at the National Netball Centre in Suva.

The final rally will be held in the Western Division on Saturday, August 29, at Lautoka Central College.

The two remaining rallies are expected to build on the participation seen in Savusavu, with teams, supporters and communities encouraged to come out and support the players as they compete at centre court.

item.title: Nadi secures win
item.description: THE McDonald’s Nadi women’s team have broken new ground in the Subrails Marama Championship, ending their winless streak against Suva with a 32-24 triumph at HFC Bank National Stadium yesterday. The Nadi side arrived in the capital high on confidence following their 89-12 demolition of Lautoka last week, but it was their fitness and willingness to attack from anywhere that proved decisive.
item.content:encoded:
THE McDonald’s Nadi women’s team have broken new ground in the Subrails Marama Championship, ending their winless streak against Suva with a 32-24 triumph at HFC Bank National Stadium yesterday.

The Nadi side arrived in the capital high on confidence following their 89-12 demolition of Lautoka last week, but it was their fitness and willingness to attack from anywhere that proved decisive.

They took the game to Suva from the opening whistle, stretching the home defence with a fast and expansive style of rugby.

Four first-half tries against Suva’s one gave Nadi a commanding 20-7 lead at halftime.

Suva refused to surrender and came out firing after the break, scoring early to turn the contest into a seesaw battle.

The visitors lifted the tempo in the final quarter, eventually pulling clear to secure a historic victory.

Nadi captain and openside flanker Laisa Seru said the team had been warned against underestimating their opponents.

“Every week the message is always not to underestimate any team,” Seru said.

“Of course the Suva girls have a lot of experience but we backed our fitness today and it paid off for us, I think.”

Seru credited the players for their determination to finish strongly.

“The coach told us just to come out here and give it our all and finish the game on a high,” she said.

“We were psyched up a little bit but we are very grateful to the girls for not giving up and finishing the game strong.”

Despite the historic win, Seru knows Nadi cannot afford to become complacent.

“Lots of positive and a lot of work still to do,” she said.

“We will go back on Monday and look at our weaknesses and get ready for the next game.”

In other Marama Championship fixtures today, Tailevu will face Nadroga at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori at 1pm. Kadavu will host Rewa at the Namalata School ground in Vunisea, also at 1pm, while Macuata takes on Ba at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka at 11am.

At Thompson Park in Navua, Namosi will host Nasinu at 1pm, while Lautoka battles Naitasiri at Churchill Park, at 11am.

item.title: North’s quest
item.description: HISTORY has taken Navatu Secondary School this far. This afternoon, the north gets its chance to demand more. When Navatu runs onto the field for its Vodafone Super Deans under-19 semi-final against Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS), it will carry something far heavier than a rugby ball and the weight of expectation.
item.content:encoded:
HISTORY has taken Navatu Secondary School this far. This afternoon, the north gets its chance to demand more.

When Navatu runs onto the field for its Vodafone Super Deans under-19 semi-final against Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS), it will carry something far heavier than a rugby ball and the weight of expectation.

It will carry the pride of an entire region.

For a school that does not have its own rugby ground or gymnasium, simply reaching the national semi-finals is an extraordinary achievement.

But Navatu is not travelling this far to make up the numbers.

The boys have already toppled one of the southern zone’s established giants Suva Grammar School.

Now they stand 80 minutes from a place in the Deans final and within touching distance of creating a moment that could change the way northern schoolboy rugby is viewed.

For principal Kiniviliame Naciqa, this journey is about much more than one rugby team.

“This victory means far more than reaching a semi-final. It represents belief, hard work, discipline, sacrifice and unity,” Naciqa said.

“It shows that northern students can compete with the best in the country and has become a source of pride and inspiration for the entire North.”

The quarter-final victory over Suva Grammar was the defining statement.

It showed that Navatu’s rise was not built on reputation or resources, but on the character of its players.

“It showed the character, resilience and belief of our boys,” Naciqa said.

“They trusted their preparation, stayed disciplined and worked for each other.”
